Storage or key registration landed without the **field schema / value-shape contract**.

That split keeps teaching implementers that `TierChanged` and `UserInteractionRequired` are the primary operational truth even though the runtime/storage owner docs have already moved to canonical event and projection families.
The Slint-facing `GraphNodeUI` and callbacks still preserve the same assumptions:
The authored sweep itself is complete and should now hand off to reconciliation rather than additional model passes.
The doc already proves that subject-first identity is viable through `preview_subject_id`; route/open ownership should align to that instead of inventing a second identity model.
The doc still uses non-deterministic phrasing in owner-level gate text:
The file still claims HITL semantics must not change, while later sections already change the meaning from request-centric tier-boundary approvals to blocked/runtime overlays.
The middle of the file still preserves stale execution ontology:
The persistence section still instructs storage to persist request-era fields that later sections explicitly demote.
Then consumer cleanup and same-file supersession collapse.
This seam is about ownership and scope, not renaming `requested_persona` back into older field families. The field names are already mostly right.
This seam is now a consumer-doc sourcing problem, not a missing-runtime-contract problem.
Usage and Evidence remain tied to `tier_id` in the canonical storage owner, which keeps recreating the same drift in Usage, Graph, and Orchestrator consumers.
`Crosswalk.md` still routes readers into stale Orchestrator and widget canon
`Formatters_System.md` continues to sit outside the central mutation/policy engine and loses attribution under DAE.
`Plugins_System.md` still permits read-only mode bypass via mutating plugin tools and env-var mutation, plus namespace/runtime model splits.
`Prompt_Pipeline.md` is upstream of requested/effective identity disclosure across chat, builders, Orchestrator, and storage. Scope drift here will keep leaking everywhere else.
`Skills_System.md` still has unresolved bundling-off semantics, compaction behavior for bundled skill text, and HTE/DAE reachability rules.
`agent-rules-context.md` still under-scopes actor coverage and execution-role inputs relative to Prompt Pipeline, Multi-Account, and Assistant chat identity disclosure requirements.
